questions.exp: Page 238 opens with 'CIN : Cervical intraepithelial neoplasia'.

questions.q: On the printed dysplasia table, LSIL on pap smear corresponds to which CIN grade?
questions.exp: The table row reads 'LSIL -> CIN 1 -> 1%'.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Fill up: The risk of cancer cervix printed against CIN 1 is ____ percent.
questions.exp: 'LSIL -> CIN 1 -> 1%' on page 238.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Which pap smear category branches into both CIN 2 and CIN 3 on the printed tree?
questions.exp: HSIL is drawn with a bracket feeding CIN 2 and CIN 3.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: The printed risk of cancer cervix for CIN 2 is:
questions.exp: 'CIN 2 -> 5%' under the HSIL arm.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Fill up: The risk range printed for CIN 3 is ____ to 40 percent.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: True/False: CIN is diagnosed on pap smear according to the printed note.
opts: False - CIN is diagnosed on colposcopy alone
False - CIN is diagnosed on HPV DNA testing
questions.exp: Page 238 states 'CIN is diagnosed on biopsy, not on pap smear'.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Odd one out - which item is NOT part of the printed CIN dysplasia table?
questions.exp: The table columns are pap smear (LSIL/HSIL), CIN (1/2/3) and risk of cancer cervix; ASC-H belongs to the pap smear inference list.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Match the pap smear category with its printed cancer risk - 1) CIN 1 2) CIN 2 3) CIN 3 ... A) 5% B) 12-40% C) 1% ... choose the correct pairing:
questions.exp: The printed risks are CIN 1 = 1%, CIN 2 = 5%, CIN 3 = 12-40%.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.unit: CIN Dysplasia Grading and Cancer Risk
questions.q: Scenario: A 32-year-old woman's pap smear reports HSIL. According to the printed dysplasia table, which CIN grades must the biopsy be read against?
questions.exp: HSIL branches to CIN 2 and CIN 3 on the page 238 tree.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: Fill up: In limited resource countries the WHO pathway runs screening, then HPV DNA plus or minus ____, then management.
questions.exp: 'Screening -> HPV DNA +/- VIA -> mx' for limited resource countries.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: Which step is printed as NOT mandatory in limited resource countries?
questions.exp: 'Biopsy is not mandatory' under the limited resource arm.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: True/False: In resource rich countries an abnormal pap smear is followed by biopsy before management.
questions.exp: 'Pap smear -Abnormal-> Biopsy -> CIN 1/2/3 -> mx' for resource rich countries.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: Odd one out - which investigation is absent from both printed WHO pathways?
questions.exp: Both WHO arms use HPV DNA, VIA, pap smear and biopsy; endometrial biopsy appears only later under AGCUS.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: The resource-rich WHO algorithm ends with management of which graded lesions?
questions.exp: The chain prints 'Biopsy -> CIN 1/2/3 -> mx'.

questions.sec: Features of CIN and WHO Guidelines on Management
questions.q: Match the country setting with its printed WHO step - 1) Limited resource 2) Resource rich ... A) Abnormal pap smear goes to biopsy B) Biopsy is not mandatory ... choose:
questions.exp: Limited resource countries skip mandatory biopsy; resource rich countries biopsy an abnormal pap.

questions.q: How many inference categories are listed under 'Inference of Pap smear' on page 238?
questions.exp: Normal, infection, LSIL, HSIL, ASCUS, ASC-H and AGCUS are listed.

questions.q: Fill up: A pap smear inference of infection is managed with ____.
questions.exp: 'Infection -> mx : Antibiotics' on page 238.

questions.q: ASC-H is expanded on the page as:
opts: Atypical squamous cells with high-grade inflammation
Atypical squamous cells where HSIL is ruled out
Atypical squamous cells of undetermined hormonal significance
Atypical squamous cells where HSIL cannot be ruled out
questions.exp: The printed expansion is 'Atypical squamous cells where HSIL cannot be ruled out (ASC-H)'.

questions.q: AGCUS stands for:
opts: Atypical squamous cells of unknown significance
Atypical glandular cells of uterine cervix significance
Atypical glandular cells of unknown significance
Atypical glandular cells with uncertain cytology score
questions.exp: 'Atypical glandular cells of unknown significance (AGCUS)' is printed.

questions.q: Which inference pair differs only by whether HSIL can be excluded?
questions.exp: ASCUS is atypical squamous cells of unknown significance while ASC-H is the subset where HSIL cannot be ruled out.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed pap smear inference line?
opts: Atypical glandular cells of unknown significance
Atypical squamous cells of known significance
questions.exp: The printed line is 'unknown significance'; a 'known significance' line does not exist.

questions.q: True/False: Normal is the first printed inference of pap smear on page 238.
questions.exp: The bullet list starts with 'Normal.'

questions.q: Which five infections are printed as diagnosable on pap smear?
opts: Candida, trichomonas, HSV, HPV and chlamydia
Bacterial vaginosis, candida, trichomonas, chlamydia and gonorrhoea
Bacterial vaginosis, candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV
Bacterial vaginosis, HSV, HPV, chlamydia and gonorrhoea
questions.exp: The 'Dx of infection in pap smear' box lists bacterial vaginosis, candida, trichomonas, HSV and HPV.

questions.q: Fill up: The two infections printed as NOT detected by pap smear are chlamydia and ____.
questions.exp: 'Infections not detected by pap smear : Chlamydia, Gonorrhea'.

questions.q: True/False: Trichomonas can be diagnosed on pap smear according to the printed lists.
opts: False - it is listed under not detected
questions.exp: Trichomonas sits in the detected list alongside bacterial vaginosis and candida.

questions.q: Odd one out - which organism belongs to the 'not detected by pap smear' list?
questions.exp: Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are the only two not detected; the rest are detected.

questions.q: Scenario: A pap smear shows clue cells and a vaginal discharge. Which printed pap-smear-detectable infection does this represent?
questions.exp: Bacterial vaginosis heads the detectable infection list and is the clue-cell disease of chapter 33.

questions.q: Match each infection with its printed pap smear detectability - 1) HSV 2) Gonorrhoea 3) Candida 4) Chlamydia ... A) Detected B) Not detected ... choose:
questions.exp: HSV and candida are detected; gonorrhoea and chlamydia are not.

questions.q: In the page 239 algorithm, an abnormal screening pap smear leads first to:
questions.exp: The flow prints 'Pap smear : Screening -Abnormal-> Per speculum examination'.

questions.q: Fill up: If per speculum examination shows a growth, the next printed step is ____ biopsy.
questions.exp: 'Growth + -> Punch biopsy' on page 239.

questions.q: When per speculum examination shows no visible abnormality, the printed next step is:
questions.exp: 'No visible abnormality -> Colposcopic guided biopsy'.

questions.q: The instrument photographed and captioned on page 239 is the:
questions.exp: The figure caption reads 'Colposcopy' under a magnifying instrument with monitor.

questions.q: Odd one out - which branch is NOT part of the page 239 abnormal pap algorithm?
opts: No visible abnormality leading to colposcopic guided biopsy
Per speculum examination after abnormal pap
Growth plus leading to punch biopsy
Direct loop excision of the transformation zone
questions.exp: The algorithm contains only examination, punch biopsy and colposcopic guided biopsy arms.

questions.q: True/False: A visible cervical growth on per speculum examination bypasses colposcopy and goes straight to punch biopsy.
opts: False - it goes to cone biopsy
False - it goes to colposcopic guided biopsy
questions.exp: The growth-positive arm ends directly in punch biopsy.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: Which two pap smear reports are managed identically at any age?
questions.exp: A bracket joins HSIL and ASC-H with the label 'Any age'.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: Fill up: LSIL at or above 25 years is managed with colposcopy plus ____ curettage.
questions.exp: 'LSIL >= 25 yrs -> Colposcopy + Endocervical curettage'.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: For ASCUS below 25 years the printed action is:
questions.exp: The age split prints '< 25 yrs : Repeat pap in 12 months' for ASCUS.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: For ASCUS above 25 years the printed action is:
opts: HPV DNA testing / reflex DNA testing
questions.exp: '> 25 yrs : HPV DNA testing / Reflex DNA testing' under ASCUS.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: LSIL in a woman younger than 25 years is managed by:
questions.exp: 'LSIL in < 25 yrs : Repeat pap in 12 months' is printed as a separate line.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: AGCUS raises suspicion of which two printed malignancies?
opts: Adenocarcinoma in situ and microinvasive cancer
Adenocarcinoma of endocervix and endometrial carcinoma spread to cervix
Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma of endocervix
questions.exp: The AGCUS bracket lists adeno carcinoma of endocervix and endometrial carcinoma spread to cervix.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: Which three procedures are printed for the AGCUS workup, in order?
opts: Colposcopic biopsy, endocervical curettage, endometrial biopsy
Colposcopic biopsy, endometrial biopsy, endocervical curettage
Punch biopsy, cone biopsy, endometrial biopsy
questions.exp: The numbered list is 1 colposcopic biopsy, 2 endocervical curettage, 3 endometrial biopsy.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: Match the pap report with its printed management - 1) ASCUS < 25 yrs 2) ASCUS > 25 yrs 3) LSIL >= 25 yrs 4) HSIL ... A) Reflex/HPV DNA testing B) Repeat pap in 12 months C) Colposcopy + endocervical curettage D) Managed at any age ... choose:
questions.exp: ASCUS under 25 repeats pap, over 25 gets DNA testing; LSIL over 25 gets colposcopy with curettage; HSIL is any age.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: Scenario: A 27-year-old woman reports ASCUS on screening. Following the printed age split, what is the next test?
opts: HPV DNA testing / reflex DNA testing
questions.exp: Above 25 years ASCUS routes to HPV DNA or reflex DNA testing.

questions.unit: Management Based on Pap Smear Reports
questions.q: True/False: LSIL at or above 25 years and LSIL below 25 years share the same printed management.
opts: False - both go to HPV DNA testing
questions.exp: LSIL >= 25 yrs goes to colposcopy with endocervical curettage while LSIL < 25 yrs repeats the pap in 12 months.

questions.q: Fill up: The colposcope is printed as a magnifying instrument of ____ times.
questions.exp: 'Magnifying instrument : x 30 times' on page 239.

questions.q: The printed focal length of the colposcope is:
questions.exp: 'Focal length : 30' on page 239.

questions.q: Which three structures does colposcopy visualise?
opts: Exocervix, transformation zone and external os
Endocervix, transformation zone and external os
questions.exp: 'Visualizes : Exocervix, Transformation zone, External os'.

questions.q: Fill up: The one region printed as NOT visualised by colposcopy is the ____.
questions.exp: 'Does not visualize : Endocervix' is indented under the visualises line.

questions.q: Which test is printed as done before colposcopy if needed?
questions.exp: 'UPT done before colposcopy if needed' on page 239.

questions.q: Colposcopy is printed as which setting of procedure?
questions.exp: 'OPD procedure' closes the colposcopy bullet list.

questions.q: Odd one out - which structure is outside the printed colposcopy field of view?
questions.exp: Only exocervix, transformation zone and external os are printed as visualised; the endocervix (and internal os) are not.

questions.q: True/False: Because colposcopy cannot see the endocervix, endocervical curettage is added when LSIL occurs at or above 25 years.
opts: False - endocervical curettage is never used
False - colposcopy sees the endocervix fully
questions.exp: The LSIL >= 25 yrs line pairs colposcopy with endocervical curettage, matching the 'does not visualize endocervix' note.

questions.q: From which areas is the colposcopic sample site chosen?
opts: Acetowhite areas only before acetic acid
questions.exp: '1. Site : Rough or pale areas' opens the samples list.

questions.q: Fill up: Applying 3-5% ____ acid on the cervix makes the biopsy taken from acetowhite areas.
questions.exp: 'Apply 3-5% acetic acid on cervix -> Biopsy taken from acetowhite areas'.

questions.q: The concentration range of acetic acid printed for colposcopy is:
questions.exp: The sampling line prints 3-5% acetic acid.

questions.q: Turning on the green filter directs biopsy from:
questions.exp: 'Green filter turned on -> Biopsy from abnormal blood vessels'.

questions.q: Which three vascular patterns branch from the green-filter step?
questions.exp: The bracket after abnormal blood vessels lists reticular, mosaic and punctate.

questions.q: Arrange the printed sampling steps in order - 1) Green filter on 2) Choose rough or pale site 3) Apply acetic acid ... choose the correct sequence:
questions.exp: The numbered list is site, then acetic acid with acetowhite biopsy, then green filter with vessel biopsy.

questions.q: Match each colposcopic aid with what it targets - 1) Acetic acid 2) Green filter ... A) Abnormal blood vessels B) Acetowhite areas ... choose:
questions.exp: Acetic acid produces acetowhite areas; the green filter reveals abnormal vessels.

questions.q: Which three inferences are printed for colposcopy on page 240?
questions.exp: The inference bullets are CIN 1/2/3, microinvasive cancers, unsatisfactory.

questions.q: Fill up: An unsatisfactory colposcopy is explained on the page as incomplete visualisation of the ____ zone.
questions.exp: The printed sub-line is 'Incomplete visualization of transition zone'.

questions.q: True/False: Microinvasive cancers are among the printed colposcopy inferences.
questions.exp: The second inference bullet is 'Microinvasive cancers'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which term is NOT a printed colposcopy inference?
opts: Satisfactory with full transformation zone seen
questions.exp: The page lists only CIN 1/2/3, microinvasive cancers and unsatisfactory.

questions.q: For CIN 1 the printed first step is:
questions.exp: The CIN 1 arm prints 'Follow up x 2-yrs'.

questions.q: If CIN 1 does not resolve on follow-up, the printed treatment is:
questions.exp: 'Does not resolve -> Cryoablation' under CIN 1.

questions.q: Fill up: The treatment of choice printed for CIN 2/3, for all age and parity, is LLETZ or ____.
questions.exp: 'CIN 2/3 : LLETZ or LEEP - mx of choice for all age & parity'.

questions.q: True/False: Hysterectomy is part of the printed management of CIN.
opts: False - it is done for CIN 3 only
False - it is done when cryoablation fails
questions.exp: The note states 'Hysterectomy is not done for CIN'.

questions.q: Odd one out - which option is absent from the printed CIN management tree?
questions.exp: The tree contains follow up, cryoablation and LLETZ/LEEP only.

questions.q: Match the CIN grade with its printed pathway - 1) CIN 1 resolves 2) CIN 1 not resolving 3) CIN 2/3 ... A) Cryoablation B) No further step printed beyond follow up C) LLETZ or LEEP ... choose:
questions.exp: Resolving CIN 1 stops at follow up, non-resolving CIN 1 is cryoablated, CIN 2/3 gets LLETZ or LEEP.

questions.q: Scenario: A 24-year-old nullipara is diagnosed with CIN 3. Which printed treatment applies irrespective of her parity?
questions.exp: LLETZ or LEEP is the printed mx of choice for CIN 2/3 for all age and parity.

questions.q: Which gases are printed as passed at very low temperature in cryoablation?
questions.exp: 'CO2/N2O passed at very low temperature' on page 240.

questions.q: Fill up: The cryogen is applied in areas of dysplasia, identified as ____ areas.
questions.exp: 'With cryogen : Applied in areas of dysplasia (Acetowhite areas)'.

questions.q: In the printed principle chain, very low temperature causes freezing of which content of dysplastic areas?
questions.exp: The chain reads 'At very low temp -> Freezing & intracellular water in dysplastic areas'.

questions.q: The end point of the cryoablation principle chain is:
questions.exp: The final box prints 'Destruction of dysplastic epithelium'.

questions.q: Give the printed freeze-thaw-freeze timings in order:
opts: Freeze 5 mins, thaw 3 mins, freeze 5 mins
Freeze 3 mins, thaw 3 mins, freeze 5 mins
Freeze 3 mins, thaw 5 mins, freeze 3 mins
Freeze 5 mins, thaw 5 mins, freeze 3 mins
questions.exp: The three boxes print freeze (3 mins), thaw (5 mins), freeze (3 mins).

questions.q: Fill up: Cryoablation destroys epithelium up to a depth of 3-____ mm.
questions.exp: 'Destruction upto 3 - 5 mm of epithelium'.

questions.q: The printed side effect of cryoablation is:
questions.exp: 'Side effect : Persistent water discharge'.

questions.q: The printed disadvantage of cryoablation is:
questions.exp: 'Disadvantage : No tissue specimen is obtained'.

questions.q: Match each cryoablation attribute with its printed value - 1) Gases 2) Cycle 3) Depth 4) Side effect ... A) 3-5 mm B) Persistent water discharge C) CO2/N2O D) 3-5-3 minutes ... choose:
questions.exp: Gases are CO2/N2O, cycle is freeze 3 thaw 5 freeze 3, depth 3-5 mm, side effect persistent water discharge.

questions.q: True/False: Cryoablation yields a tissue specimen for histopathology.
opts: False - it yields fluid for culture
questions.exp: The printed disadvantage is that no tissue specimen is obtained.

questions.q: How many criteria must all be fulfilled before cryoablation in CIN 1?
questions.exp: The prerequisites list four bullets: entire TZ visible, lesion completely visible, not HIV +ve, lesion not > 2 quadrants.

questions.q: Fill up: The entire ____ should be visible before cryoablation is done in CIN 1.
questions.exp: 'Entire TZ should be visible' heads the prerequisites.

questions.q: Which HIV status is printed as acceptable for cryoablation in CIN 1?
questions.exp: 'Not be HIV +ve' is the third prerequisite.

questions.q: The lesion must not involve more than how many quadrants of the cervix?
questions.exp: 'Lesion not > 2 quadrants of cervix' closes the list.

questions.q: Odd one out - which is NOT a printed cryoablation prerequisite?
questions.exp: The prerequisites are visibility of TZ and lesion, HIV negativity and lesion within 2 quadrants; cryoablation is for CIN 1.

questions.q: True/False: A CIN 1 lesion spanning three quadrants of the cervix still satisfies the printed prerequisites for cryoablation.
questions.exp: The lesion must not exceed 2 quadrants.

questions.q: Fill up: In LLETZ/LEEP the total ____ area is removed.
questions.exp: 'Total dysplastic area is removed' opens the LLETZ block.

questions.q: What is passed into the LLETZ instrument according to the printed chain?
questions.exp: The chain prints 'Current -passed into-> Instrument'.

questions.q: The loop in LLETZ is printed to:
opts: Cut and coagulate at the same time
questions.exp: 'Cut & coagulate at the same time' follows the instrument box.

questions.q: The printed duration of the LLETZ procedure is:
questions.exp: 'Short procedure : 10-15 mins' under advantage.

questions.q: Up to what depth are tissues removed in LLETZ?
questions.exp: 'Tissues removed until 10 mm depth'.

questions.q: LLETZ is printed as the treatment of choice for which grades, at any age and parity?
questions.exp: 'TOC for CIN 2 & 3 for any age & parity'.

questions.q: Which advantage allows histopathology after LLETZ but not after cryoablation?
opts: Tissue sample can be sent for HPE
questions.exp: The indented note under TOC is 'Tissue sample can be sent for HPE', unlike cryoablation.

questions.q: The printed disadvantage of LLETZ is:
questions.exp: 'Disadvantage : Bleeding (minimal)'.

questions.q: LLETZ shares which setting advantage with colposcopy?
questions.exp: Both lists print 'OPD procedure'.

questions.q: Match each LLETZ attribute with its printed value - 1) Energy 2) Time 3) Depth 4) Disadvantage ... A) 10 mm B) Minimal bleeding C) Current D) 10-15 mins ... choose:
questions.exp: Current is passed into the loop, the procedure lasts 10-15 mins, depth is 10 mm and bleeding is minimal.

questions.q: The figure captioned on page 241 with panels A to F shows:
questions.exp: The six-panel photograph is captioned 'LLETZ'.

questions.q: In special scenario 1, a positive endocervical curettage leads next to:
questions.exp: The chain prints 'Endocervical curettage positive -> Cone biopsy'.

questions.q: Fill up: In special scenario 1, cone biopsy revealing adenocarcinoma in situ ends in ____.
questions.exp: 'Adenocarcinoma in situ -> Hysterectomy' closes scenario 1.

questions.q: In special scenario 2, a pap smear of HSIL is followed by:
questions.exp: 'PAP smear : HSIL -> Colposcopy & biopsy' opens scenario 2.

questions.q: Which colposcopic biopsy results create the printed 'discrepancy in reports' in scenario 2?
questions.exp: 'Colposcopy & biopsy : CIN 1 or Normal' with the arrow labelled discrepancy in reports.

questions.q: The discrepancy in scenario 2 is resolved by:
questions.exp: The arrow from discrepancy in reports ends at cone biopsy.

questions.q: Arrange scenario 1 in printed order - 1) Adenocarcinoma in situ 2) Endocervical curettage positive 3) Hysterectomy 4) Cone biopsy ... choose:
questions.exp: The printed chain is curettage positive, cone biopsy, adenocarcinoma in situ, hysterectomy.

questions.q: Scenario: A 40-year-old with HSIL pap has colposcopic biopsy reading CIN 1. According to the printed special scenario, what should be done next?
opts: Accept the CIN 1 and follow up
questions.exp: HSIL pap against CIN 1 biopsy is the printed discrepancy that mandates cone biopsy.

questions.q: True/False: Adenocarcinoma in situ found on cone biopsy is managed by hysterectomy in the printed scenario.
questions.exp: Scenario 1 ends 'Adenocarcinoma in situ -> Hysterectomy'.

questions.q: Fill up: In cone biopsy a ____ shaped area of cervix is cut.
questions.exp: 'Cone shaped area of cervix is cut' on page 241.

questions.q: Which three zones must the cone include?
opts: Exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone and endocervix
questions.exp: The 'To include' list is exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone, endocervix.

questions.q: Cone biopsy is performed in which setting?
questions.exp: 'Done in OT under GA' closes the cone biopsy bullets.

questions.q: The cone biopsy diagram on page 241 labels which three cervical regions from above down?
questions.exp: The figure leader lines read endocervix, TZ, ectocervix.

questions.q: Odd one out - which structure is NOT inside the printed cone specimen?
questions.exp: The cone includes exo/ecto cervix, transformational zone and endocervix only.

questions.q: True/False: Unlike colposcopy and LLETZ, cone biopsy needs the operating theatre and general anaesthesia.
opts: False - it needs only local anaesthesia
False - it is an OPD procedure
questions.exp: 'Done in OT under GA' contrasts with the OPD label on colposcopy and LLETZ.

questions.q: Which three diagnostic indications for cone biopsy are printed on page 242?
opts: Suspecting adenocarcinoma or adenocarcinoma in situ, poorly visualised TZ on colposcopy, and discrepancy in pap smear and colposcopy reports
Microinvasive cancer, visible growth, and positive punch biopsy
Suspecting squamous cancer, satisfactory colposcopy, and concordant reports
HSIL pap, ASCUS pap and AGCUS pap
questions.exp: The diagnostic bullets list exactly those three indications.

questions.q: Fill up: A poorly visualised ____ on colposcopy is a printed diagnostic indication for cone biopsy.
questions.exp: 'Poorly visualised TZ on colposcopy' is the second diagnostic bullet.

questions.q: The therapeutic indications place cone biopsy as management of Ca cervix in which group?
questions.exp: 'Mx of Ca cervix in young females' heads the therapeutic bullets.

questions.q: Which FIGO stage is printed as microinvasive Ca under the therapeutic indication?
questions.exp: The sub-bullet prints 'Stage IA : microinvasive Ca'.

questions.q: Cone biopsy gives evidence of what key feature in the therapeutic list?
questions.exp: 'Evidence of microinvasion' is the last therapeutic bullet.

questions.q: Match each cone biopsy indication class with its printed items - 1) Diagnostic 2) Therapeutic ... A) Evidence of microinvasion, mx of Ca cervix in young females B) Suspected adenocarcinoma in situ, poorly visualised TZ, discrepant reports ... choose:
questions.exp: The diagnostic arm lists suspicion of adenocarcinoma in situ, poor TZ view and report discrepancy; the therapeutic arm lists microinvasion and young females.

questions.q: P-16 protein testing is invoked when the pap smear shows confusion between which two categories?
questions.exp: The flow prints 'Confusion between LSIL & HSIL : Indeterminate'.

questions.q: An increased p-16 protein result points to:
questions.exp: The raised arrow arm is labelled HSIL.

questions.q: Fill up: A normal p-16 protein result leaves the report as ____.
questions.exp: The normal arm of the p-16 tree ends at LSIL.

questions.q: Arrange the p-16 pathway in printed order - 1) P-16 protein 2) Pap smear 3) Indeterminate confusion between LSIL and HSIL 4) HSIL or LSIL answer ... choose:
questions.exp: Pap smear precedes the indeterminate confusion, then p-16 protein, then the HSIL or LSIL split.

questions.q: Scenario: A pap smear cannot decide between LSIL and HSIL and p-16 staining is strongly increased. The printed inference is:
questions.exp: The upward arrow from p-16 leads to HSIL when the protein is raised.

questions.q: True/False: A normal p-16 result downgrades the indeterminate report towards LSIL.
questions.exp: The normal arm of the printed tree terminates at LSIL.
